series.title: Why we published the dose card
series.dek: A discount gives you nothing to be curious about. A formula does.

series.title: Why it's a stick pack, not a capsule
series.dek: Three grams of inositol is nine capsules. Nobody takes nine capsules.

decision.considered: Capsule format, six to nine capsules per daily serving
decision.rejected: Daily capsule count at an honest inositol dose · a format that reduces the dose by making it tedious
decision.revisitIf: We ship a formula whose full daily dose fits into three capsules

series.title: The fiber decision
series.dek: We wanted it in. The texture, and the honesty about dose, kept it out.

decision.considered: Inulin or a viscous fiber, 1–5 g per serving
decision.rejected: An honest dose does not fit a 5 g serving · viscosity changes the drink · a token gram would be a marketing dose
decision.revisitIf: We make a format where serving size is not the binding constraint

series.title: Why there's no berberine
series.dek: The most requested ingredient we left out. Three reasons, one unflattering.

decision.rejected: GI tolerability at an effective dose · CYP3A4 interaction profile · mechanism outside this formula's job
decision.revisitIf: We ship a separate capsule format where dose and timing can be controlled

series.pullQuote: If an ingredient only makes the label longer, it is not an ingredient. It is copywriting.

series.title: Why there's no caffeine
series.dek: You don't need a spike at 3pm. You need the edge taken off.

series.title: What "clinically studied" actually means
series.dek: Studied at what dose, in whom, for how long, and by whom.

changeLog.summary: Saffron extract dose set at 28 mg after supplier standardisation confirmed.
Myo-inositol fixed at 3,000 mg, down from a 4,000 mg option, to keep one scoop drinkable.
Added fiber removed from the formula. Reasoning published as article 03.
